summary: Lane 8 resolved with wire-verified sources. (1) FIELD MAPPING: "State" -> TIGER STATE (STATEFP/STUSPS); "District" has NO US equivalent and must be renamed COUNTY (5-digit state+county FIPS GEOID, TIGER's county layer already covers Louisiana parishes / Alaska boroughs as county-equivalents); "PIN Code" -> 5-digit ZIP, whose only free polygon approximation is the Census ZCTA. The Census Bureau itself states USPS ZIP Codes are assigned to delivery routes and are "a point-based dataset unsuitable for mapping and many analysis applications" — so ZIP-from-coordinate is inherently an approximation, and Census also warns "Not all valid ZIP Codes are represented by a 2020 ZCTA" and that uninhabited areas over two square miles may be left unassigned — which is exactly where rural interstate truck shops live, so ZIP legitimately NULLs out ("unknown") for some rows. (2) REVERSE GEOCODING: I verified the Census Geocoder coordinates endpoint works keyless (HTTP 200, returned Kent County GEOID 10001 + ZCTA 19901 + STATE 10 for a Delaware point), but there is NO coordinate-batch endpoint (geographies/coordinatebatch = 404; only addressbatch exists, capped at 10,000 records/file) and I measured 1.23-1.57 s per single call — meaning ~39 hours single-threaded for 100k shops. The recommendation is therefore decisively OFFLINE TIGER-in-PostGIS: I verified tl_2025_us_county.zip (83,989,800 B) and tl_2025_us_zcta520.zip (529,118,424 B) both resolve, are public domain, and give unlimited zero-ToS-risk ST_Contains lookups; use the Census Geocoder only as a low-volume spot-check/reconciliation oracle. Nominatim is PROHIBITED for this use: its policy explicitly lists "Systematic queries ... reverse queries in a grid" under Unacceptable Use and says "If you need complete sets of data, get it from the OSM planet or an extract." (3) ADDRESS NORMALIZATION: usaddress (MIT, released 2025-08-07) and pypostal/libpostal (MIT, released 2025-10-29) are maintained; usaddress-scourgify (MIT, last release 2023-12-14) is the USPS-Pub-28 standardizer but is going stale — and there is a real footgun I verified: the PyPI package literally named `scourgify` is a Calibre fanfiction tag normalizer, NOT the address library. (4) JUNCTIONS: there is NO free federal national interchange inventory. I checked FAF5 Network Nodes (974,788 points) which does have Interchange/Exit_Number fields, but only 4,485 rows are populated and every sample is a "Toll Road Entry/Exit Point" — toll plazas, not interchanges; NHPN is polyline-only with no exit-node concept. The only viable source is OSM highway=motorway_junction: I measured 77,676 nodes in the US (vs 237,971 globally per taginfo), of which 48,424 carry a `ref` = 62.3% exit-number coverage, so nearest_junction_ref must NULL for the other ~37.7%. (5) INTEGRATION PREMISE CORRECTION: the brief says the repo's OSM pipeline is "highway-WAYS-only today", but scripts/osm_extract.py already runs a streaming pyosmium NODE|WAY pass with a TagFilter that produces osm.fuel_stations / rest_areas / weigh_points from nodes — so adding motorway junctions is ~30 lines riding the SAME PBF pass, not a new pipeline. (6) ODbL: ingesting all 77,676 US junctions is a "systematic attempt to aggregate all ... Primary Features of a given type" under the OSMF Geocoding Guideline, so share-alike attaches — which is precisely why the existing ruling §3.1-4a (OSM lives only in osm.*, joined at query time) must hold for junctions too, while TIGER-derived state/county/ZIP stay public-domain and ODbL-free.

sources.name: Census TIGER/Line 2025 — County shapefile (national)
sources.license: U.S. Government work / public domain (17 U.S.C. §105). No attribution obligation, no share-alike.
sources.us_coverage: national (all states, DC, PR, island areas; includes county-equivalents: LA parishes, AK boroughs/census areas)
sources.why_it_matters: THE recommended source for the County field (the correct US mapping of 'District'). Loaded into PostGIS once, gives unlimited offline ST_Contains point-in-polygon county assignment with zero ToS risk and zero rate limit.
sources.caveats: Content-Length verified = 83,989,800 bytes (~80 MiB); Last-Modified Tue, 23 Sep 2025. TIGER is cartographic/statistical boundary data, not legal survey boundaries.

sources.name: Census TIGER/Line 2025 — ZCTA5 (2020 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas) shapefile
sources.license: U.S. Government work / public domain (17 U.S.C. §105).
sources.us_coverage: national, but NOT total-area — uninhabited land/water areas over two square miles may be unassigned
sources.why_it_matters: The only free authoritative POLYGON approximation of ZIP Codes — this is what fills the 'PIN Code' -> ZIP field offline. Point-in-polygon in PostGIS.
sources.caveats: Content-Length verified = 529,118,424 bytes (~504 MiB); Last-Modified Tue, 23 Sep 2025. HONESTY-CRITICAL: a ZCTA is NOT a ZIP Code. Census states 'All 2020 ZCTA Codes are current valid USPS ZIP Codes (as of January 1, 2020). Not all valid ZIP Codes are represented by a 2020 ZCTA.' and 'Uninhabited areas (land and water areas) over two square miles are potentially left unassigned from 2020 ZCTA coverage' — rural interstate shops can legitimately fall outside every ZCTA, in which case zip MUST be NULL (renders 'unknown'), never guessed from the nearest polygon. ZCTAs are frozen at the 2020 Census; they do not track USPS ZIP changes since.

sources.name: Census TIGER/Line 2025 — State shapefile
sources.why_it_matters: Fills the 'State' field. Smallest of the three files — verified 9,954,307 bytes (~9.5 MiB), Last-Modified 2025-06-27.
sources.caveats: I verified the 2024 vintage URL specifically (9,954,307 B). The TIGER2025/ directory listing also returns 200, so tl_2025_us_state.zip is expected to exist by the same naming convention, but I did NOT range-check that exact filename — treat the 2025 state filename as [UNVERIFIED] until checked. State can also be derived from the county GEOID's first 2 digits, making a separate state layer optional.

sources.name: Census TIGER/Line 2024 — County + ZCTA (prior vintage, for reproducibility pinning)
sources.why_it_matters: Vintage pinning matters for the repo's honesty rules: observed_at for an admin-field assignment should be the TIGER VINTAGE year, not the download date. Verified sizes: county 2024 = 83,913,260 B, zcta520 2024 = 528,806,468 B, both Last-Modified 2025-06-27.
sources.caveats: Boundaries change between vintages (county name/FIPS changes are rare but real, e.g. Connecticut's 2022 planning-region conversion). Pin the vintage in the source registry.

sources.name: Census ZCTA-to-County relationship file (2020)
sources.why_it_matters: Lets you sanity-check ZIP<->county consistency for a shop (a ZCTA can straddle county lines) and flag rows where the derived ZIP and county are geographically implausible — a cheap quality signal for the confidence score.
sources.caveats: Relationship, not geometry. Many ZCTAs legitimately span multiple counties, so a mismatch is not automatically an error.

sources.name: Census Geocoder API — coordinates -> geographies (reverse geocode)
sources.license: U.S. Government work / public domain. No API key, no registration.
sources.us_coverage: United States, Puerto Rico, and U.S. Island Areas (per official docs)
sources.why_it_matters: I actually called it: for x=-75.5244,y=39.1582 it returned Counties GEOID 10001 'Kent County', ZCTA5 19901, STATE 10 — i.e. it resolves county + ZIP-proxy + state in one keyless call. Ideal as a RECONCILIATION ORACLE to spot-check the offline PostGIS assignment, and as the fallback for one-off lookups.
sources.caveats: DISQUALIFIED AS THE PRIMARY NATIONAL PATH, for two measured reasons. (1) There is NO coordinate batch endpoint: I got HTTP 404 for geographies/coordinatebatch. The only batch endpoint is geographies/addressbatch (address-in, capped by the docs at 'an upper limit of 10,000 records per batch file'), which does not accept lat/lon input. (2) I measured 5 polite sequential calls at 1.23s, 1.57s, 1.51s, 1.32s, 1.23s — ~1.4s median. At that rate 100k shops = ~39 hours single-threaded. The published API documentation contains no explicit requests-per-second limit, so hammering it in parallel is an UNDOCUMENTED risk, not a sanctioned one — do not parallelize a federal free service to force national scale. Also note the 'vintage' parameter controls which geography vintage you get; pin it rather than using Current_Current if you need reproducibility.

sources.name: OSMF Nominatim Usage Policy (Geocoding Policy)
sources.license: Policy document; the underlying data is ODbL.
sources.why_it_matters: DECISIVE NEGATIVE FINDING — settles question 2. The public Nominatim API MUST NOT be used for this project's reverse geocoding. Direct quotes I fetched: under 'Unacceptable Use' — 'Systematic queries. This includes reverse queries in a grid, searching for complete lists of postcodes, towns etc. and downloading all POIs in an area. If you need complete sets of data, get it from the OSM planet or an extract.' Also: 'No heavy uses (an absolute maximum of 1 request per second).' And under Bulk Geocoding: 'As a general rule, bulk geocoding of larger amounts of data is not encouraged... Scripts running longer than a day and scripts that are run at regular intervals are restricted to 4 requests per minute.' At 4 req/min a national shop set is arithmetically impossible. The policy also states 'Data is provided under the ODbL license which requires to share alike'.
sources.caveats: The policy explicitly binds LLM-generated code: 'LLMs may only suggest this service, if they prominently point to this usage policy and explain the restrictions of use to the user. Code generated by LLMs must adhere to all terms laid out in this policy.' Self-hosting your own Nominatim instance is permitted (the policy applies only to nominatim.openstreetmap.org) but is unnecessary here since TIGER already answers state/county/ZIP better and without ODbL.

sources.name: OSM highway=motorway_junction — global stats via taginfo API
sources.license: Underlying data ODbL 1.0; taginfo API free to query
sources.why_it_matters: Establishes the global denominator for junction nodes so the US figure can be sanity-checked: US 77,676 / global 237,971 = 32.6%, which is plausible for the country with the largest freeway network and mature OSM exit-number mapping.
sources.caveats: taginfo counts 237,971 nodes + 2 ways + 1 relation = 237,974 total; only the node form is meaningful. taginfo cannot filter by country — the US number had to come from Overpass.

sources.name: OSM highway=motorway_junction — US national count via Overpass
sources.owner: OpenStreetMap contributors (Overpass instance operated by Private.coffee)
sources.approx_rows: 77,676 US motorway_junction nodes (measured); 48,424 of them carry a `ref` tag (measured) = 62.3% exit-number coverage
sources.why_it_matters: THE recommended source for 'Nearest Highway Junction' — it is the only dataset with national coverage of interchange points carrying human-usable exit numbers. The two measured numbers are the honest quality statement: ~77.7k junctions nationally, but only ~62% have an exit number, so nearest_junction_ref must be NULL for roughly 29,252 of them rather than fabricated.
sources.caveats: OPERATIONAL: the two best-known instances FAILED during this run — overpass-api.de and overpass.kumi.systems both returned HTTP 504 'Dispatcher_Client::request_read_and_idx::timeout. The server is probably too busy'. overpass.osm.ch returned a count of 0 for a US bbox (it is not a global instance). Only overpass.private.coffee answered. This instability is itself the argument for ingesting from the PBF rather than depending on Overpass at runtime. LICENSING: bulk-ingesting all 77,676 is a systematic aggregation and triggers ODbL share-alike (see OSMF Geocoding Guideline row).

sources.name: Geofabrik United States OSM extract (us-latest.osm.pbf)
sources.license: ODbL 1.0 — attribution to OpenStreetMap contributors + share-alike on derived databases
sources.approx_rows: unknown (file is 12,038,018,063 bytes = ~11.2 GiB, measured via range request; Last-Modified Wed, 22 Jul 2026 22:52:44 GMT)
fields_provided: all OSM nodes/ways/relations incl. highway=motorway_junction with ref/name
sources.why_it_matters: This is the source the repo ALREADY uses (sql/schema_wave2.sql comments it as 'Geofabrik US PBF -> osm.*'). Junctions should ride the exact same file and the exact same osmium pass — no new download, no new dependency, no Overpass runtime dependency.
sources.caveats: Requires -L (I measured a 302 redirect before the 206). The per-state extract path also works and is far smaller for dev (delaware-latest.osm.pbf = 21,814,984 bytes, measured), which matches the repo's current Delaware-only osm.* bbox and makes a cheap smoke test.

sources.name: OSMF Licence Community Guideline — Geocoding
sources.why_it_matters: Settles the first-class ODbL question for THIS lane. Quoted from the page I fetched: 'A collection of Geocoding Results is not a substantial extract of the OSM database provided: 1. only names, addresses, and/or latitude/longitude information are included in the Geocoding Results, and 2. the collection is not a systematic attempt to aggregate all or substantially all Primary Features of a given type (as defined in the Collective Database Guideline) within a geographic area city-sized or larger.' Ingesting all 77,676 US motorway_junction nodes plainly FAILS test 2 — it is a systematic aggregation of every Primary Feature of that type nationally. Therefore junctions are a substantial extract and share-alike attaches.
sources.caveats: CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REPO: this vindicates and extends existing ruling §3.1-4a. osm.motorway_junctions belongs in the osm.* schema alongside fuel_stations/rest_areas/weigh_points, joined at query time, and must never be merged into core.* (whose CHECK constraint already forbids present_in='osm'). Conversely, because state/county/ZIP come from public-domain TIGER and NOT from OSM, those three published fields carry zero ODbL obligation — that clean separation is worth stating explicitly in the README.

sources.name: NTAD Freight Analysis Framework (FAF5) Network Nodes
sources.owner: USDOT Bureau of Transportation Statistics / FHWA
sources.license: Verified from item metadata: 'This NTAD dataset is a work of the United States government as defined in 17 U.S.C. § 101 and as such are not protected by any U.S. copyrights. This work is available for unrestricted public use.'
sources.why_it_matters: This is the ONLY federal dataset I found with fields literally named Interchange and Exit_Number, so it had to be checked properly rather than dismissed — and checking it produced a clear NEGATIVE result that saves the build team from a wrong turn.
sources.caveats: DOES NOT WORK as a national interchange inventory. Measured: of 974,788 nodes only 4,485 have Interchange NOT NULL, 3,102 have Exit_Number NOT NULL, 4,472 have Entry_or_Exit NOT NULL. I pulled 6 sample rows and every single one was Facility_Type='Toll Road Entry Point' or 'Toll Road Exit Point' (e.g. Interchange='MAY AVE', Facility_Name='KILPATRICK TURNPIKE'), and State was NULL on all of them. These are TOLL PLAZA access points, not general freeway interchanges. Coverage is ~4.5k vs OSM's 77.7k. Useful only as a niche toll-facility cross-reference, not for the nearest_highway_junction field. maxRecordCount=2000, so paginate.

sources.name: NTAD National Highway Planning Network (NHPN)
sources.license: NTAD: U.S. government work, not protected by U.S. copyright, unrestricted public use.
sources.why_it_matters: Checked specifically to rule it out as a junction source, and to flag it as a strong candidate for the MISSING ROUTES TABLE. It is esriGeometryPolyline with no exit-node concept (CONN_ID/CONN_DES are connector-link attributes, not interchanges), so it cannot fill nearest_highway_junction. BUT its ROUTE_ID + SIGN1/SIGNT1/SIGNN1 + LRS milepost fields are exactly the vocabulary a federal, public-domain, ODbL-free core.routes table would need — which matters because the ground truth says no routes table exists yet.
sources.caveats: Route-table suitability is my architectural read, not a verified build — treat the 'use NHPN for core.routes' suggestion as a recommendation to evaluate, not a settled finding. Also compare against National Highway Freight Network (NHFN, item 55a0298bd1744857834cd49ce1a8bbfe) and HPMS 2024 (item 5e6a977c2d7c4ec1bdc82e684d3384f2, distributed as File Geodatabase with no FeatureServer url), both of which I confirmed exist with the same NTAD public-domain licence.

sources.name: usaddress (DataMade) — CRF-based US address parser
sources.why_it_matters: MAINTAINED and the right first choice for PARSING a US address string into components before you standardize it. Measured: PyPI version 0.5.16 uploaded 2025-08-07; GitHub 1,631 stars, last push 2025-08-07, not archived, MIT.
sources.caveats: It PARSES (labels tokens), it does not STANDARDIZE to USPS Pub 28 form and it does not validate that an address exists. It is a probabilistic CRF model — it returns a best-guess tag sequence and can mislabel unusual strings, so it should emit a confidence/flag rather than being trusted silently. Pure-Python, trivial install.

sources.name: libpostal + pypostal — international address parsing/normalization
sources.why_it_matters: The strongest normalizer for messy/heterogeneous input (which scraped shop addresses will be) and the best at address EXPANSION (e.g. 'St'/'Street', 'N'/'North') for dedupe matching. Measured: repo 4,850 stars, last push 2026-05-13, not archived, MIT. Python bindings `postal` 1.1.11 uploaded 2025-10-29 — actively released.
sources.caveats: MAINTENANCE NUANCE worth being honest about: the repo is active (pushed 2026-05-13) but the latest TAGGED RELEASE is still v1.1 from 2018-05-09 — so you are effectively building from master. OPERATIONAL COST: it is a C library requiring a compile toolchain plus a ~2GB+ trained model download at install — noticeably heavier than usaddress, and awkward in slim containers. Its training data is derived substantially from OpenStreetMap, so if you are being strict about ODbL provenance, note that libpostal's MODEL is OSM-derived even though the library is MIT.

sources.name: usaddress-scourgify — USPS Pub 28 address standardizer
fields_provided: postal_code (normalized to USPS Pub 28 / RESO conventions)
sources.why_it_matters: This is the answer to 'USPS-style standardization WITHOUT the USPS API' — its stated purpose is literally 'Clean US addresses following USPS pub 28 and RESO guidelines'. It wraps usaddress and outputs the standardized shape.
sources.caveats: TWO WARNINGS. (1) STALENESS: PyPI 0.6.0 uploaded 2023-12-14; GitHub last push 2024-01-26, 241 stars. Not archived, but ~2.5 years without a release — pin the version and own the risk. (2) NAMING FOOTGUN I VERIFIED ON PyPI: the package named plain `scourgify` (version 1.4.0, uploaded 2026-07-11) is a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT project — its summary is 'Normalize and consolidate tags/fandoms/characters/genres in a FanFicFare-imported Calibre library' (github.com/elfensky/scourgify). `pip install scourgify` installs the wrong thing and it is actively published, so it looks fresh and legitimate. The correct install is `pip install usaddress-scourgify`. Also note Pub 28 standardization is FORMATTING only — it does not verify deliverability; only USPS's own address API does that.

sources.name: Census Geocoder Services API documentation
sources.us_coverage: US, Puerto Rico, U.S. Island Areas
sources.why_it_matters: Primary evidence for the batch limit and the benchmark/vintage semantics. Direct quote extracted: 'There is currently an upper limit of 10,000 records per batch file.' Also documents that returntype=geographies accepts a `layers` parameter (comma-delimited by ID or name from the TIGERweb WMS layer list) so you can request only Counties + ZCTAs + States instead of `all` and cut response size substantially.
sources.caveats: The documentation does NOT publish a requests-per-second rate limit. Absence of a documented limit is NOT permission to parallelize — treat the measured ~1.4s/call as the practical ceiling and stay single-threaded.

sources.name: Census ZIP Code Tabulation Areas (ZCTAs) — official guidance page
sources.why_it_matters: THE citation for the honest ZIP caveat the repo README should carry. Verbatim quotes I pulled: 'The USPS assigns ZIP Code ranges to regional post offices, which in turn assign ZIP Codes to delivery routes. Each delivery route is composed of street networks, and/or individual units with high mail volumes... The result is a point-based dataset unsuitable for mapping and many analysis applications.' and 'ZCTAs are generalized areal representations of the geographic extent and distribution of the point-based ZIP Codes built using 2020 Census tabulation blocks.'
sources.caveats: Also documents the delineation rules that create real NULLs: 'Not all valid ZIP Codes are represented by a 2020 ZCTA', 'Uninhabited areas (land and water areas) over two square miles are potentially left unassigned from 2020 ZCTA coverage', '2020 ZCTAs may form noncontiguous areas', and ZCTAs may represent PO-Box-only or firm-specific ZIPs. Every one of these is a legitimate reason for zip=NULL on a rural highway shop.

sources.name: TIGERweb REST services (Current vintage)
fields_provided: county / ZCTA / state / place layers with identify + query
sources.why_it_matters: Third free path (besides offline TIGER and the Geocoder API) — a queryable spatial service for ad-hoc identify calls, and the authority for the `layers` IDs the Geocoder's layers parameter accepts.
sources.caveats: Same objection as the Geocoder for national scale: it is a network round-trip per point. Use offline PostGIS instead; keep this for debugging.

recommendations: FIELD RENAMES — do this before any code is written, because the India vocabulary will otherwise get baked into the schema. 'District' -> `county_name` + `county_fips` (5-digit state+county GEOID, e.g. 10001). There is NO US administrative unit called a district that is equivalent; county is the correct second-level unit, and TIGER's county layer already includes county-EQUIVALENTS (Louisiana parishes, Alaska boroughs and census areas, independent cities like St. Louis and Baltimore, DC), so a single layer covers 100% of US territory with no special-casing. 'PIN Code' -> `zip5` (CHAR(5), keep the leading zero — store as TEXT, never INTEGER, or 01234 becomes 1234). 'State' -> `state_usps` (2-letter) + `state_fips`. 'WhatsApp Number' should be dropped or NULL-by-default for the US — WhatsApp is not a meaningful business-contact channel for US truck repair shops and there is no free legal source for it.

PRIMARY REVERSE-GEOCODE PATH = OFFLINE TIGER IN POSTGIS. Load tl_2025_us_state.zip, tl_2025_us_county.zip, tl_2025_us_zcta520.zip into a `tiger` schema via shp2pgsql or ogr2ogr, add GIST indexes, and assign admin fields with ST_Contains. Rationale is measured, not aesthetic: the Census Geocoder has no coordinate-batch endpoint (I got 404 on geographies/coordinatebatch) and clocked ~1.4s per single call, so 100k shops = ~39 hours of hammering a free federal service; the same 100k points against an indexed PostGIS polygon table is seconds. Offline also means zero ToS risk, zero rate-limit risk, deterministic reproducibility, and it works when the network is down. Total disk cost is ~615 MB of downloads.

ALWAYS USE ST_Contains, NEVER 'nearest polygon'. If a shop's coordinate falls in no ZCTA, `zip5` MUST be NULL and render as 'unknown' — do not snap it to the nearest ZCTA. Census explicitly warns that uninhabited areas over two square miles may be unassigned, which is precisely the rural-interstate geography where truck repair shops cluster. Silently snapping would manufacture a false ZIP and violate the repo's NULL-means-unknown rule. Add a flag like 'zip_outside_zcta_coverage' so the gap is visible rather than mysterious.

SET observed_at CORRECTLY FOR DERIVED ADMIN FIELDS. The county/ZIP of a coordinate was 'true in the world' as of the TIGER VINTAGE (2025), not as of your download. So observed_at for these fields = the TIGER vintage date, and source_id should encode the vintage (e.g. 'census_tiger_2025_county'). Pin the vintage in the registry rather than always pulling 'latest', otherwise a re-run silently changes published values with no lineage explanation.

USE THE CENSUS GEOCODER AS A RECONCILIATION ORACLE, NOT THE PIPELINE. Sample a few hundred rows per run, call the keyless coordinates endpoint, and assert the offline PostGIS county/ZCTA match. Disagreements are a real quality signal (bad geometry load, wrong SRID, vintage drift). Keep it single-threaded with a sleep, route it through the existing polite_get() choke point, and log every call to ops.source_runs like any other fetch. Pass layers=Counties,States,2020 Census ZIP Code Tabulation Areas instead of layers=all to cut the payload.

DO NOT USE NOMINATIM AT ALL for this project. Its policy explicitly classes grid/systematic reverse queries as Unacceptable Use and caps recurring scripts at 4 requests/minute, which makes national coverage arithmetically impossible even if it were permitted. Add an explicit note in the repo (README or the source registry) recording this decision and the policy URL, so a future contributor does not 'helpfully' add it. If someone later wants OSM-quality addresses, the legal route is self-hosting Nominatim from the PBF you already download — not the public API.

ADDRESS NORMALIZATION STACK — recommend usaddress (parse) + usaddress-scourgify (standardize to USPS Pub 28), with libpostal/pypostal reserved for messy or ambiguous inputs. usaddress is genuinely maintained (released 2025-08-07) and pure-Python. usaddress-scourgify is the only free Pub-28 standardizer but is stale (last release 2023-12-14) so PIN THE VERSION. Add libpostal only if measured parse failure rates justify its ~2GB model and C toolchain; note its latest tagged release is still v1.1 from 2018 despite an active master branch.

GUARD AGAINST THE scourgify TYPOSQUAT-BY-COINCIDENCE. `pip install scourgify` gets a Calibre fanfiction tag normalizer (PyPI 1.4.0, published 2026-07-11 — it looks fresh and legitimate), NOT the address library. The correct package is `usaddress-scourgify`. Write the correct name in pyproject.toml with a comment explaining the trap, because the import name is `scourgify` while the install name is `usaddress-scourgify`, which is exactly how this mistake happens.

STATE PLAINLY THAT PUB-28 STANDARDIZATION IS NOT VALIDATION. usaddress-scourgify reformats a string; it does not confirm the address exists or is deliverable. Only USPS's own address API can do that, and it requires registration with ToS restricting use to mailing purposes — so under this project's no-paid-keys/fully-legal constraint, `address_verified` should be NULL/unknown, and the confidence score should reflect 'formatted' not 'verified'.

NEAREST HIGHWAY JUNCTION = OSM highway=motorway_junction, ingested from the Geofabrik PBF the repo ALREADY downloads. There is no free federal alternative — I checked and ruled out FAF5 Network Nodes (its Interchange/Exit_Number fields are populated on only 4,485 of 974,788 rows and every sample is a toll plaza) and NHPN (polyline, no exit-node concept). OSM gives 77,676 US junction nodes with ref (exit number) and name.

CORRECTION TO THE TASK BRIEF: the repo's OSM pipeline is NOT 'highway-WAYS-only today'. scripts/osm_extract.py already runs a streaming pyosmium pass with entities=NODE|WAY and a TagFilter, producing osm.fuel_stations, osm.rest_areas and osm.weigh_points FROM NODES. So adding junctions is a small symmetric change, not new infrastructure: add ('highway','motorway_junction') to the _MATCH_TAGS tuple, add a branch to the _kind() dispatcher, and create osm.motorway_junctions modeled exactly on osm.fuel_stations (osm_id, ref, name, geom Point 4326, source_id, run_id, ingested_at, observed_at from the PBF osmosis_replication_timestamp, confidence sub-scores, flags, props JSONB). It rides the SAME single PBF pass and the SAME disk-based node-location cache — no extra download, no extra runtime cost, no Overpass dependency.

PUBLISH THE 62.3% EXIT-NUMBER COVERAGE HONESTLY. 48,424 of 77,676 US junction nodes carry a `ref`. For the other ~29,252, nearest_junction_ref MUST be NULL ('unknown') while nearest_junction_name or the raw node id can still be populated. Consider exposing two distinct fields — nearest_junction_ref (exit number, often NULL) and nearest_junction_distance_m (always computable) — so a NULL exit number does not destroy an otherwise useful answer.

DO NOT DEPEND ON OVERPASS AT RUNTIME. During this research overpass-api.de AND overpass.kumi.systems both returned HTTP 504 'the server is probably too busy'; overpass.osm.ch silently returned 0 for a US bbox (it is regional, so a naive caller would have recorded 'zero junctions in the USA' as a fact). Only overpass.private.coffee answered. Use Overpass strictly for ad-hoc research and cross-checks, ingest production data from the PBF, and if any Overpass call ever does land in the pipeline it must treat a 0 result as SUSPECT rather than authoritative.

KEEP JUNCTIONS IN osm.* AND JOIN AT QUERY TIME — ruling §3.1-4a applies with full force. Per the OSMF Geocoding Guideline, bulk-ingesting all 77,676 US junctions is 'a systematic attempt to aggregate all or substantially all Primary Features of a given type' and is therefore a substantial extract carrying ODbL share-alike. Do NOT copy junction ref/name into a core.* published row as a materialized column; compute nearest_junction via a query-time join against osm.motorway_junctions, exactly as the existing architecture does for fuel/rest/weigh. This is the same discipline core.businesses already enforces with its present_in <@ ARRAY['overture','fsq'] check.

STATE THE CLEAN LICENCE SPLIT IN THE README. state/county/ZIP come from Census TIGER = US Government public domain, no attribution required, NO share-alike, freely publishable. Junction ref/name come from OSM = ODbL, attribution required, share-alike on the derived database. Because these are different fields from different schemas, the admin fields are ODbL-free and can be served without contaminating anything — but only if nobody merges the two into one physical table. Make that explicit so the boundary survives future contributors.

TRAVEL DIRECTION — implement as a DERIVED, LOW-CONFIDENCE, USUALLY-NULL field, and rename it to something honest like `access_from_direction` with a companion `access_direction_basis` explaining how it was inferred. The only defensible meaning for a FIXED shop is: which carriageway / direction of travel can reach it without a U-turn or a long detour. Derivation: snap the shop to the nearest osm.ways segment within a small threshold; if that way is oneway=yes and part of a divided-highway pair, the direction of travel is derivable from the way's geometry direction combined with its ref/name directional suffix. Emit it ONLY when that chain is unambiguous.

SET access_from_direction TO NULL (unknown) IN ALL OF THESE CASES, and treat that as the expected common outcome rather than a failure: (a) nearest road is undivided/bidirectional, i.e. no oneway tag — both directions reach it, so direction is meaningless; (b) the oneway tag is simply absent — untagged is UNKNOWN, never 'no', per the repo's honesty rule; (c) the shop is on a surface street off the highway and reached via the local network, where carriageway has no bearing; (d) the nearest interchange is a full diamond/cloverleaf serving both directions; (e) snap distance exceeds the confidence threshold. Because most truck repair shops sit on frontage roads and surface streets rather than directly on a freeway carriageway, expect this field to be NULL for the large majority of rows — and that is the correct, defensible result, not a data gap to be filled by guessing.

NEVER PRESENT access_from_direction AS AN OBSERVED FACT. It is inferred from geometry, so its observed_at must be the OSM extract timestamp of the underlying way (not a survey date), it must carry a reduced confidence sub-score, and it should be flagged (e.g. 'derived_from_geometry'). It is the single most fabrication-prone field in the whole requested list — a plausible-looking 'Northbound' that is actually wrong will send a stranded driver to the wrong side of a divided highway. If in doubt, NULL it.

EVALUATE NHPN AS THE BASIS FOR THE MISSING core.routes TABLE. The ground truth says no routes table exists anywhere, yet the whole enrichment task is defined as 'for every truck route'. NHPN is federal, public-domain (no ODbL), national, polyline, and carries ROUTE_ID, SIGN1/SIGNT1/SIGNN1 (route signing), LNAME, NHS and STRAHNET flags, plus LRS mileposts — i.e. exactly the route_id/route_name vocabulary the per-shop fields require, and using it keeps routes ODbL-free. Compare against the National Highway Freight Network (a truck-specific subset, arguably the better fit for a TRUCK intelligence platform) before committing. Flagging this as a blocking dependency: the buffer/distance/nearest-route-point fields cannot be built until routes exist.

ORDER OF OPERATIONS for the enrichment job, so the cheap deterministic steps gate the expensive ones: (1) load TIGER into PostGIS; (2) assign state/county/ZIP by ST_Contains — fast, offline, no NULLs except genuine coverage gaps; (3) ingest osm.motorway_junctions in the existing PBF pass; (4) build core.routes from NHPN/NHFN; (5) buffer routes and select candidate shops; (6) compute nearest junction and distance-from-route via query-time joins; (7) attempt access_from_direction last, expecting mostly NULL; (8) standardize address strings with usaddress + usaddress-scourgify; (9) spot-check a sample against the Census Geocoder and log the agreement rate as a quality metric.

unfillable_or_risky.problem: There is no US administrative unit called a 'district' at this level. The field name is imported from India's administrative hierarchy and has no US referent — US 'districts' that do exist (congressional districts, school districts, judicial districts) are entirely different things and would be actively misleading if populated here.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Rename to county_name + county_fips and fill from Census TIGER county shapefile (public domain, verified live, 83,989,800 bytes). TIGER's county layer already includes all county-equivalents (Louisiana parishes, Alaska boroughs/census areas, independent cities, DC) so coverage is complete with no special-casing.

unfillable_or_risky.field_or_claim: PIN Code / true USPS ZIP Code for a coordinate
unfillable_or_risky.problem: A USPS ZIP Code is a set of mail DELIVERY ROUTES, not a polygon — Census states plainly that within MAF/TIGER, ZIP Codes are 'a point-based dataset unsuitable for mapping and many analysis applications'. Therefore no coordinate can be authoritatively converted to a USPS ZIP using free polygon data; any ZIP you derive is an approximation. Additionally, USPS's own authoritative address/ZIP API requires registration and its ToS restricts use to mailing purposes, so it is off-limits under this project's constraints.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Use the Census ZCTA polygon (TIGER tl_2025_us_zcta520.zip, verified 529,118,424 bytes, public domain) via ST_Contains, and label the field honestly in the schema/docs as a ZCTA-derived approximation of ZIP. Emit NULL when the point falls outside all ZCTA coverage — Census warns that uninhabited areas over two square miles may be unassigned, and that 'Not all valid ZIP Codes are represented by a 2020 ZCTA'. Never snap to the nearest ZCTA.

unfillable_or_risky.problem: 2020 ZCTAs are frozen at the 2020 Census and were built from ZIP Codes valid as of January 1, 2020. USPS has changed ZIP assignments since. So a ZCTA-derived zip5 can be stale relative to the real world by several years, and there is no free authoritative feed of USPS ZIP changes.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Publish the ZCTA vintage explicitly in source_id and set observed_at to the ZCTA vintage (2020 delineation / 2025 TIGER release), never the download date. Accept staleness openly rather than implying currency; flag zip5 with a 'zcta2020_derived' marker so downstream consumers can reason about it.

unfillable_or_risky.field_or_claim: National interchange / exit inventory from a federal source
unfillable_or_risky.problem: No such free federal dataset exists. I verified the closest candidates and both fail: NTAD FAF5 Network Nodes has literal Interchange/Exit_Number fields but only 4,485 of 974,788 rows populate Interchange, 3,102 populate Exit_Number, and every sampled row is Facility_Type='Toll Road Entry/Exit Point' (toll plazas, e.g. KILPATRICK TURNPIKE) with State=NULL; NHPN is esriGeometryPolyline with no exit-node concept at all (CONN_ID/CONN_DES are connector-link attributes).
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: OSM highway=motorway_junction — 77,676 US nodes measured via Overpass. Accept the ODbL consequence: keep it in the osm.* schema and join at query time, never materialized into core.*, consistent with existing ruling §3.1-4a.

unfillable_or_risky.problem: Only 48,424 of 77,676 US motorway_junction nodes carry a `ref` tag (both numbers measured this run) — 62.3% coverage. Roughly 29,252 junctions have no exit number in OSM at all. There is no free source to backfill the remainder nationally.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Populate nearest_junction_ref where OSM has it, NULL ('unknown') where it does not, and always populate nearest_junction_distance_m and (where available) nearest_junction_name so the record stays useful without the exit number. Optionally cross-reference individual state DOT open-data portals for specific corridors, but do not promise national backfill.

unfillable_or_risky.field_or_claim: Travel Direction for a fixed shop
unfillable_or_risky.problem: The field is conceptually ill-posed as written — a stationary building has no travel direction. Any value is an INFERENCE about which carriageway can reach it, derived from OSM way geometry and oneway tagging, not an observed fact. It is highly fabrication-prone and a wrong value has real safety/utility cost (sending a stranded driver to the wrong side of a divided highway).
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Rename to access_from_direction, derive only when the shop snaps unambiguously to a oneway=yes divided-carriageway segment, carry a companion access_direction_basis explaining the inference, assign a reduced confidence sub-score and a 'derived_from_geometry' flag, set observed_at to the OSM extract timestamp, and NULL it whenever the road is undivided, oneway is untagged, access is via the local street network, the junction serves both directions, or the snap distance exceeds threshold. Expect NULL for the majority of rows and treat that as correct.

unfillable_or_risky.problem: Free Pub-28 standardization (usaddress-scourgify) only REFORMATS a string into USPS conventions — it does not confirm the address exists or is deliverable. Genuine verification requires the USPS address API, which needs registration and whose ToS limits use to mailing purposes, putting it outside this project's no-paid-keys / fully-legal constraint.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Keep address_verified NULL/unknown. Expose a separate address_standardized boolean reflecting only that formatting succeeded, and let the confidence score reflect 'formatted, not verified'. Never let a standardized-looking address imply validation.

unfillable_or_risky.problem: India-vocabulary field with essentially no US applicability — US truck repair shops do not publish WhatsApp as a business contact channel, and there is no free legal US source for it in any case.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Drop the field, or retain it NULL-by-default and document that it is out of scope for a US-only platform. Do not derive it from the phone number — a US landline is not a WhatsApp account, and asserting one would be fabrication.

unfillable_or_risky.problem: Explicitly prohibited by the OSMF Nominatim Usage Policy. 'Systematic queries. This includes reverse queries in a grid... If you need complete sets of data, get it from the OSM planet or an extract' appears under Unacceptable Use, and recurring scripts are capped at 4 requests/minute, which makes national coverage impossible even setting the prohibition aside.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Offline Census TIGER in PostGIS for state/county/ZIP (public domain, unlimited, no ToS risk), with the keyless Census Geocoder used only as a low-volume reconciliation spot-check. If OSM-derived addressing is ever genuinely needed, self-host Nominatim from the Geofabrik PBF the repo already downloads.

unfillable_or_risky.field_or_claim: Census Geocoder as the national reverse-geocoding pipeline
unfillable_or_risky.problem: No coordinate-batch endpoint exists (geographies/coordinatebatch returned HTTP 404; only addressbatch exists and it takes addresses, not lat/lon, capped at 10,000 records per file). Measured single-call latency was 1.23-1.57s across 5 polite sequential calls, implying ~39 hours for 100k shops single-threaded. The docs publish no requests-per-second limit, so parallelizing to compensate would be an undocumented imposition on a free federal service rather than sanctioned use.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Offline TIGER PostGIS point-in-polygon as the primary path; reserve the Geocoder for sampled reconciliation, routed through polite_get() and logged to ops.source_runs like every other fetch.

open_questions: BLOCKING DEPENDENCY: there is still no routes table anywhere in the repo, yet every requested field is defined relative to 'every truck route' (route id, route name, distance from route, nearest route point). Which route universe is authoritative — NHPN (broadest, federal, public-domain), the National Highway Freight Network (truck-specific, arguably the correct fit for a TRUCK platform), HPMS 2024, or OSM ways already in osm.ways? This must be decided before buffer/distance/nearest-point work can start, and the choice has licence consequences: NHPN/NHFN keep routes ODbL-free, OSM does not.

Should the admin fields (state/county/zip) live as materialized columns on the shop row, or be computed at query time like the OSM joins? They are public-domain TIGER so there is no licence reason to keep them out of core.*, and materializing is far faster — but it means a TIGER vintage bump silently changes published values unless the vintage is part of source_id and a re-run is triggered. Recommend materializing WITH vintage-stamped lineage, but the repo owner should rule.

What is the buffer distance actually measured against — the route centerline geometry, or road-network travel distance? A shop 500m from an interstate as the crow flies may be 8km by road if there is no nearby interchange. The requested field is named 'distance from route' which reads as straight-line, but the useful number for a stranded driver is drive distance. Straight-line is free and easy with PostGIS; drive distance needs a routing engine (Valhalla is already noted as the Phase 3 moat). Which one ships first, and should both be exposed as separate fields?

TIGER vintage policy: pin to 2025 permanently, or track latest annually? Pinning gives reproducibility and stable observed_at; tracking gives currency. Related: I verified tl_2025_us_county.zip and tl_2025_us_zcta520.zip directly, but for the STATE layer I only range-checked the 2024 filename — the TIGER2025/ directory returns 200 so tl_2025_us_state.zip almost certainly exists, but that exact filename is [UNVERIFIED] and should be range-checked before being written into the registry.

Does the project want per-state TIGER files or the national ones? National county is 80 MiB and national ZCTA is 504 MiB, which is fine to load once. But if the ingest is ever sharded by state (mirroring the current Delaware-only osm.* bbox), per-state TIGER files exist and would cut dev-loop time substantially — worth deciding alongside the OSM backfill strategy.

How should ODbL attribution actually surface in the product? The guideline requires crediting OpenStreetMap under ODbL §4.3 wherever OSM-derived junction data is publicly used. Is that a footer line on the API docs, a per-response attribution field, or a licence endpoint? And should API responses carry per-field provenance so a consumer can tell that county came from TIGER (free to reuse) while nearest_junction_ref came from OSM (share-alike)? That distinction is the whole reason the schemas are kept separate and it currently has no user-visible expression.

The US OSM backfill is dead (no process, no systemd timers) and osm.* still covers only Delaware. Adding motorway_junction to _MATCH_TAGS is cheap, but the 11.2 GiB national PBF pass is not — what is the plan and machine budget for the national osmium run, and should junctions be added to the tag filter BEFORE that run so it only has to happen once rather than twice?

Confidence scoring for derived admin fields: what conf_trust / conf_complete / conf_agree values should a TIGER point-in-polygon assignment get? It is deterministic and authoritative, so arguably maximum trust — but the ZCTA layer is a documented approximation of ZIP, so zip5 should plausibly score lower than county_fips even though both came from the same load. Needs an explicit rule so the numbers mean something.
